facts.fact_text: Hyde Park (the first applicant) continued staging protests and demonstrations after removal from the Government's list of non-governmental organisations.

On 10 February 2006, Hyde Park (the first applicant) applied to the Chişinău Municipal Council for authorisation to hold a peaceful demonstration in front of the Parliament building on 25 February 2006.
On 21 February 2006, the Chişinău Municipal Council rejected Hyde Park's (the first applicant's) application to hold a demonstration in front of the Parliament building on 25 February 2006.
On 24 February 2006, the Chişinău Court of Appeal dismissed the applicants' action challenging the Chişinău Municipal Council's refusal to authorise the demonstration.
On 28 June 2006, the Supreme Court of Justice dismissed the applicant's appeal on points of law against the Chişinău Court of Appeal's judgment of 24 February 2006.

Section 12(6) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the local authorities can reject an application to hold an assembly only if, after having consulted the police, they have obtained convincing evidence that the provisions of sections 6 and 7 of the Assemblies Act will be breached with serious consequences for society.

Section 14(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that a decision rejecting the application for holding an assembly shall be reasoned and presented in writing, and shall contain reasons for refusing to issue the authorisation.
